main_text.l: talis uentriculus eft præditus. Hæc autem
uis à spiritus animalis subtilitaꝛe procedit:
uel hoc uitij debilitati naturali uentriculi,
qui acria tolerare nequit, tribuendum est.
Vndénam autem orta sit hęc innata debili-
tas, non loga inuestigatione opus est: cùm
ea sit oportet alicuius intemperiei, uentri-
culi symptoma. Omnem enim similarium
partium imbecillitatē,
alicui intemperiei
acceptam hactenus omnes medici tum ue
teres, tum recentiores retulerunt. Potest e-
tiam attribui eximia hæc sentiendi facul-
tas cuidam proprietati, quæ à quadam de-
finita temperatione originem duxit. Non
enim omnium uentriculorum hominum
uniforme ac idem temperametum est, sed
pro diuersa elementorum permistione, ip-
sum quoq; uariat. Idem quoque de ijs, qui
nonnullis odoribus magnopere, uel iuuan
tur, uel læduntur, existimare par est. Iuuan-
tur enim uel læduntur mutato temperamen-
to. Quòd insuper iecoris & uentriculi affec-
tus præter naturam astringentia remedia
perpetuò postulet, non propterea illarum
partium materias quibusdam morbis affi-
ci consequitur. Nam hæc duo uiscera astrin-
gentibus gaudent, non quatenus similares
partes

page.notes: Marginal references in the right margin: "III." beside the first paragraph's line about odoribus, and "IV." beside the line about astringentia remedia; each stands as a marginal mark, not as text. Doubtful readings: "subtilitaꝛe" and "temperametum" read as printed; "cùm ea sit oportet" is printed as shown. Running head and page number taken from the top line. Printed words in the text kept as printed, including the printed hyphenations "debili-tas", "intemperiei", "facul-tas", "defi-nita", "astrin-gentibus" that were broken at the line ends.
